items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Region of Waterloo’s Municipal Speed Camera Program
notes: Doug Spooner, Acting Transportation Commissioner, Region of Waterloo gave a presentation outlining the Region’s municipal speed camera and administrative penalties program, including an overview of the current program and the upcoming expansion, an explanation of community safety zones, and the Region’s communications plan. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-17,
notes: Aminu Bello gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, including an overview of the current subject property and the requested zoning by-law amendments.
He then responded to questions of Council. Bob Henderson also responded to questions of Council.

Michael Witmer, Senior Planner, GSP Group Inc. gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development and zoning by-law amendments, including some resident comments. He then responded to questions of Council.
Kerry Church, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the petition signed by her neighbours against this development, as well as the community in the area.
Saba Mirzaagha, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the development community and how development decisions get made.

Jalud Abdulmenan, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the zoning in the neighbourhood and how that impacted their decision to buy a home there, as well as road safety. Aminu Bello responded to questions of Council.
Naz Rahim, Resident of Waterloo spoke about the community in the neighbourhood, and the lack of integration from the development.
Sunny Lubana, Owner spoke about the desire to keep trees on the site, as well as to develop relationships with the community.
Allison Henshall, Resident of Waterloo spoke about her concerns with the proposal, including the traffic issues, noise, garbage collection and the wildlife in the area.

Roger Joudrie, Resident of Waterloo spoke about infrastructure concerns in the area, as well as concerns for his children that currently live at the property. Aminu Bello responded to questions of Council.

Kimberly Cyr, Resident of Waterloo shared some concerns about the grading at the new development and its relation to her property. She also spoke about the snow banks, parking, and the utilities. She then responded to questions of Council. Aminu Bello responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Informal Public Meeting and indicated that staff will review the issues and report back to Council at a later date.

items.title: Official Plan Amendment 51,
notes: Amanda Wyszynski gave a presentation outlining the proposed development, including the site specific zoning exemptions. She then responded to questions of Council.
Jeff Henry, Urban Planner, Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc. gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development. He then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Councillor Freeman having previously declared a pecuniary interest was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Wright wanted to speak about a hate-motivated incident that occurred in Uptown last week, and the overarching issue of hate crimes in the Region. She mentioned that there is a motion coming to Council next week regarding combatting hate in the community.

Mayor McCabe echoed the sentiments and spoke about the actions different groups are taking to combat hate in the Region, including those by the City, while acknowledging there is still more work to be done.

Councillor Hanmer wanted to congratulate St. Mary’s General Hospital, which opened on October 21, 1924 and is celebrating 100 years. The Region of Waterloo Ken Seiling Museum has an exhibit called Beyond the Bricks open until April 2025 about the legacy of the hospital.

Councillor Bodaly hosted an information session for a new park block in the extended development for Vista Hills. He is grateful to staff for connecting with the developer and their planner to host and for communicating with residents in the area.

Councillor Roe wanted to highlight that the Waterloo Professional Firefighters Association held their graduation for new firefighters on Friday, October 18th. It was a great day to welcome them and their families, and see the dedication and commitment they have.
Mayor McCabe wanted to commemorate the two years since becoming Mayor and since the election. It’s been a journey of learning and she thanked everyone for their help.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report COM2024-037. 2. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund (CSRIF) grant program – Stream 1 Repair and Rehabilitation for the proposed project AMCC Revitalization and Accessibility Retrofit with a project value of $1,550,000. 3. That if the City of Waterloo’s AMCC Revitalization and Accessibility Retrofit grant application is successful, Council approves the required City portion of $775,000 be funded as follows: a. $100,000 from the Accessibility Facility Upgrades (Ref#130) b. $500,000 from the Grant Opportunities (Ref#146) c. $50,000 from the Building Capital Renewal Program (Ref#229) d. $125,000 from the Large-Scale Programming Specialties (Ref#337) 4. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund (CSRIF) grant program – Stream 2 New Builds, Signature New Builds for the proposed project RIM Park Diamonds 4, 5 and 6 Upgrades and Expansion with a project value of $7,800,000. 5. That if the City’s RIM Park Diamonds 4, 5 and 6 Upgrades and Expansion grant application is successful, Council approves the required City portion of $3,900,000 be funded as follows: a. $448,000 from Outdoor Sports Field Strategy implementation Project 160008 (Ref# 291) b. $198,000 from the Park Shade Structure Project (Ref#294) c. $1,940,000 from RIM Park Ball Diamond Upgrades (Ref #297) and that this 2026 non-routine funding be released on January 1, 2026. d. $1,098,000 from the Artificial Turf Replacement Project (Ref#311) e. $216,000 from Playground Upgrades/Expansion City Wide Project 110083 (Ref#324) 6. That Council authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign the grant transfer agreement and any other related documents, subject to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor.

1. That Council approve report COM2024-037.

2. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund (CSRIF) grant program – Stream 1 Repair and Rehabilitation for the proposed project AMCC Revitalization and Accessibility Retrofit with a project value of $1,550,000.

3. That if the City of Waterloo’s AMCC Revitalization and Accessibility Retrofit grant application is successful, Council approves the required City portion of $775,000 be funded as follows: a. $100,000 from the Accessibility Facility Upgrades (Ref#130) b. $500,000 from the Grant Opportunities (Ref#146) c. $50,000 from the Building Capital Renewal Program (Ref#229) d. $125,000 from the Large-Scale Programming Specialties (Ref#337)

4. That Council approve the City of Waterloo’s grant application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund (CSRIF) grant program – Stream 2 New Builds, Signature New Builds for the proposed project RIM Park Diamonds 4, 5 and 6 Upgrades and Expansion with a project value of $7,800,000.

5. That if the City’s RIM Park Diamonds 4, 5 and 6 Upgrades and Expansion grant application is successful, Council approves the required City portion of $3,900,000 be funded as follows: a. $448,000 from Outdoor Sports Field Strategy implementation Project 160008 (Ref# 291) b. $198,000 from the Park Shade Structure Project (Ref#294) c. $1,940,000 from RIM Park Ball Diamond Upgrades (Ref #297) and that this 2026 non-routine funding be released on January 1, 2026. d. $1,098,000 from the Artificial Turf Replacement Project (Ref#311) e. $216,000 from Playground Upgrades/Expansion City Wide Project 110083 (Ref#324)

6. That Council authorize the Mayor and Clerk to sign the grant transfer agreement and any other related documents, subject to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor.
